about: The chapter, hymn, and versicle are omitted. The celebrant sings Et valde mane, and the cantors continue the antiphon. Incensation takes place during the Benedictus as at Lauds. After the doxology, the whole antiphon is repeated before the postcommunion prayer.

seg.tr: And very early in the morning
on the first day of the week, they come to the tomb, with the sun already risen, alleluia.

a.g: on the first day of the week

ex.w004: The phrase names the first day of the week.
ex.w009: The sun has already risen when they reach the tomb.

seg.tr: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, for He has visited and redeemed His people,
and raised up saving power for us in the house of David, His servant,

ex.w025: The horn is an image of strength. Here it expresses the power that brings salvation in David’s house.

seg.tr: as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets who lived long ago:

a.g: of His holy prophets who lived long ago

ex.w038: Holy describes the prophets, whose phrase resumes after the words about their life long ago.

seg.tr: to free us from our enemies and from the grasp of all who hate us,

ex.w055: Their hatred is present. The Latin verb uses perfect forms for this continuing state.

seg.tr: to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant:
the oath He swore to Abraham, our father: He would grant us this:

ex.w068: The oath specifies the covenant just mentioned.
ex.w074: God’s oath promises a gift: the freedom to serve Him without fear.

seg.tr: that, freed from our enemies’ grasp, we might serve Him without fear,

ex.w084: Those freed are the people who will serve God, not the enemies.

seg.tr: in holiness and justice before Him all our days.
And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare His ways,

a.g: will be called a prophet of the Most High

ex.w097: Zacharias addresses his son John, who will prepare the Lord’s way.

seg.tr: to give His people knowledge of salvation in the forgiveness of their sins,

ex.w118: Salvation is described here in relation to the forgiveness of the people’s sins.

seg.tr: through the tender mercy of our God, by which the Rising Light from on high will visit us,

a.g: the Rising Light will visit us

ex.w122: The bodily image expresses God’s deep compassion.
ex.w126: Which refers to God’s mercy: that mercy brings the visitation.
ex.w129: The title evokes rising light. It names the one who will illuminate those in darkness in the following words.

seg.tr: to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.

a.g: sit in darkness and in the shadow of death

seg.tr: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit,
as it was in the beginning, so it is now and always, forever and ever. Amen.
And very early in the morning, on the first day of the week, they come to the tomb, with the sun already risen, alleluia.

a.g: on the first day of the week
